title: Impact of Medicare Eligibility on Hospital Visits

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).

Why: Medicare eligibility turns on deterministically at the 65-year threshold. By comparing individuals immediately below and above the age cutoff we obtain a locally randomized experiment. The running variable is age (scaled 0–1 in this file) and treatment jumps from 0 to 1 at the cutoff (≈ 0.5).  

Key assumptions  
• Continuity: In the absence of Medicare, the conditional expectation of log hospital visits is smooth in age at the cutoff.  
• No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot precisely choose their age, so density of the running variable is continuous at the threshold.  
• Stable composition: No other policies change exactly at age 65 within the narrow window used.

## 2. R Code
```r
# ----- 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------------
needed <- c("readr", "dplyr", "rdrobust", "ggplot2")
new_pkgs <- needed[!(needed %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new_pkgs)) install.packages(new_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(rdrobust); library(ggplot2)

# ----- 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s86_data.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE)

# ----- 2. Basic inspection ---------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.5   # treatment turns on at running_var >= 0.5

# ----- 3. Main RDD estimate --------------------------------------------------
rdr <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
cat("\nMain rdrobust estimate (local linear, MSE-optimal h):\n")
print(rdr)

# Extract point estimate for reporting
tau_hat  <- rdr$Estimate[1]      # conventional local-linear effect
se_hat   <- rdr$se[1]
p_val    <- rdr$pv[1]
cat(sprintf("\nPoint estimate (τ̂): %.4f  |  SE: %.4f  |  p-value: %.3f\n",
            tau_hat, se_hat, p_val))

# ----- 4. Robustness checks --------------------------------------------------

## 4a. Use half and double the optimal bandwidth
h_opt <- rdr$bws[1,1]                # MSE-optimal bandwidth from rdrobust
for(h in c(h_opt/2, h_opt*2)){
  tmp <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h)
  cat(sprintf("\nBandwidth %.3f → τ̂ = %.4f (SE %.4f)\n",
              h, tmp$Estimate[1], tmp$se[1]))
}

## 4b. Higher-order polynomial (quadratic)
rdr_quad <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)
cat("\nQuadratic specification → τ̂ =", round(rdr_quad$Estimate[1],4),
    " (SE", round(rdr_quad$se[1],4), ")\n")

## 4c. Placebo cutoff at 0.3 (should be insignificant)
placebo <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = 0.3)
cat("\nPlacebo cutoff 0.3 → τ̂ =", round(placebo$Estimate[1],4),
    " (p-value", round(placebo$pv[1],3), ")\n")

# ----- 5. Graphical diagnostic ----------------------------------------------
ggplot(df, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed") +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm",
              formula = y ~ poly(x,1),
              data = subset(df, running_var < cutoff),
              se = FALSE, colour = "blue") +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm",
              formula = y ~ poly(x,1),
              data = subset(df, running_var >= cutoff),
              se = FALSE, colour = "red") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Log hospital visits around Medicare eligibility",
       x = "Running variable (age, rescaled 0–1)",
       y = "log(hospital visits)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic priors and prior RDD work (e.g. Card, Dobkin & Maestas 2019) show that Medicare increases inpatient utilization at age 65. Therefore we expect a positive jump in log hospital visits. Magnitude: roughly +0.05–0.10 log points (≈ 5–10 % more visits) with statistical significance; robustness checks should yield similar, positive estimates and placebo tests should be null.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare individuals just below and above age 65.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Medicare eligibility at age 65 leads to a reduction in hospital visits.
